subject: Copywriting
title: The Gutenberg Moment
description: A fast breakdown of The Gutenberg Moment for builders.

hook.text: In 1440, Gutenberg invented the printing press. Within decades, the first printed advertisements appeared.

buildup.text: William Caxton printed the first English ad in 1477—a flyer for Easter prayer books at his shop.

discovery.text: Printing made ads scalable. One message could reach thousands. The economics of persuasion changed forever.

twist.text: Early printers hated ads. They saw their craft as noble. Commerce felt beneath them. Money won.

climax.text: By 1600, handbills covered London. Ads for medicines, shows, and services wallpapered every surface.

punchline.text: The printing press didn't just spread ideas. It sold them.

quiz.question: Who printed the first known English advertisement?

details.summary: Gutenberg's printing press (c. 1440) transformed advertising from individual handbills to mass-produced commercial messages. The first printed English advertisement appeared around 1477, promoting books. Print made advertising scalable for the first time, enabling merchants to reach thousands...
details.whyItMatters: The printing press was advertising's first technological disruption — the internet of the 15th century. Each subsequent disruption (radio, TV, digital) followed the same pattern of democratizing access to audiences.
takeaways: The printing press made mass advertising possible for the first time
William Caxton printed the first known English advertisement around 1477
Print technology reduced the cost of reaching large audiences dramatically

faq.question: What was the first printed advertisement?
faq.answer: William Caxton printed a handbill around 1477 advertising religious books for sale at his Westminster print shop. The text was straightforward: here is what's available, here is where to buy it. Advertising copy began as pure information.

faq.question: How did the printing press change advertising?
faq.answer: It made mass production of identical messages possible for the first time. Before print, each advertisement was handwritten or carved individually. Print reduced costs, increased reach, and standardized messaging — the same advantages digital technology later brought.
